acceptance_criteria.statement: ReconcileExecution handles both an indeterminate observation and an orphaned executing record with no durable provider-invocation observation.
Recovery first calls get_execution_outcome with the stored logical execution identity after current path-Workspace and WorkspaceResourceAuthorizer checks.

ObservationReferenceResolver.resolve_started_execution validates the immutable AuthorizedExecutionBindingSnapshot against proposal/execution state and resolves only the trusted opaque routing handle; it creates no write authority.

Provider observation and terminal finalization remain allowed after original proposal/reference expiry or key revocation when current Workspace/resource observation authorization passes; missing or mismatched snapshot/trusted-store state remains typed non-terminal and never becomes failed.

Any provider retry reruns full m4r1 side-effect verification, current Workspace/resource authorization, ExecutionAuthorizer and exact capability/binding/policy compatibility; expired or revoked reference/key and material mismatch forbid retry and require new proposal/approval.
takeover_stale_execution uses PostgreSQL time, exact expected generation and a strictly expired lease; Applied increments generation once and changes owner/deadline atomically.
Current lease returns ExecutionNotStale, changed generation returns ExecutionFenced, terminal state returns persisted outcome, and stale owners cannot observe or finalize after takeover.
record_execution_observation and finalize_execution enforce exact current owner/generation plus unexpired lease and expose only approved typed outcomes.
Crash after provider commit but before Knora persistence reconciles provider-authoritative success or closed failure without a duplicate side effect.

Crash after Knora persists executing but before provider receipt stays non-terminal, observes not-found, takes over only when stale, and retries with the same stored logical ID/fingerprint only after all current write checks pass.

provider_observation_unavailable, timeout and unknown/malformed observed outcome map to ReconciliationIndeterminate HTTP 202; provider not-found maps to distinct ProviderOutcomeNotFound HTTP 202; neither terminalizes or grants retry authority.
Only found(succeeded) or found(failed(closed_code)) may finalize; closed failure maps to 502/TOOL_PROVIDER_FAILURE.

SQLite provider state/idempotency survives Knora restart independently of ToolActionStore, and recovery, takeover, authorization, observation, retry, fencing and finalization are reconstructable from append-only audit.

design_decisions.decision: Keep ReconcileExecution behind WriteProposalWorkflow.handle; callers cannot orchestrate observe, takeover, retry, admission or finalization.

Separate current observation authorization from write authority. Observation may resolve trusted routing for an already-started execution after expiry/revocation, but a provider write reruns every current execution and compatibility check.
Observe provider-owned SQLite truth before any takeover or retry decision. Point-in-time not-found is non-terminal and cannot retire an outstanding admission.
Use PostgreSQL compare-and-swap takeover with fresh post-lock database time, expected generation and strict lease expiry; generation and owner fence every later observation/finalization.

NoAdmission may create the first admission only after full current write authorization; AdmissionOutstanding may only replay the byte-identical persisted envelope. Both reuse the immutable logical execution ID and fingerprint.
Provider not-found, unavailable, timeout and malformed/unknown observations remain typed non-terminal. Only closed provider outcomes may finalize.
Retain the static typed capability registry and provider-owned reference boundary; do not add plugins, dynamic discovery or a vendor-specific integration.

invariants: Every provider observation follows current path-Workspace and resource-observation authorization.
Observation/read authority never constructs an admission envelope and never grants provider-write authority.
Every retry reruns current execution authority, exact approved capability/binding/policy compatibility and complete m4r1 write validity.
Provider truth is read before takeover or retry; provider not-found is never interpreted as failed.
One immutable logical execution ID and fingerprint survive every generation and retry.
At most one admission exists per logical execution; AdmissionOutstanding replay is byte-identical.
Concurrent takeover has one atomic winner; stale owners cannot append an observation or terminal outcome.
Reference/proposal expiry blocks a new write start or retry but does not block authorized observation/finalization of an already-started execution.
SQLite remains authoritative for external outcome and idempotency independently of PostgreSQL ToolActionStore.
Raw provider routing, envelope bytes, credentials, key material and authority secrets never enter public or audit projections.
out_of_scope: Dynamic plugins, capability discovery, runtime provider registration or a vendor marketplace.
Editing an immutable proposal or silently reusing approval after material capability, binding, policy or target change.
Distributed transaction, cross-store rollback or provider-atomic cancellation.
M4.5 integrated release harness and final M4 fixed-point code review, owned by Issue #79 and the final feature gate.

test_cases.statement: Seed executing AdmissionOutstanding states whose SQLite outcome is success or each closed rejection while PostgreSQL has no observation, then reconcile before lease expiry and after restart.
test_cases.oracle: Provider truth is observed first, exactly one authorized current owner records one observation/audit and finalizes success to succeeded or the named rejection to failed; no provider write occurs and restart reconstructs the same result.

test_cases.statement: Seed executing NoAdmission after Knora persisted acquisition but before admission/provider receipt; observe provider not-found before and after strict lease expiry, race takeover contenders, then authorize retry.
test_cases.oracle: Not-found remains HTTP 202 and non-terminal. Before expiry takeover returns ExecutionNotStale. After expiry exactly one expected-generation contender atomically increments generation/owner/deadline, reruns all current write checks, creates the first admission and dispatches once with the original logical ID/fingerprint; losers make zero provider calls.

test_cases.statement: Seed AdmissionOutstanding with provider not-found, expire its lease, race authorized replay with a delayed original owner and concurrent takeover contenders.
test_cases.oracle: One takeover wins; retry reuses the exact persisted envelope and never creates another admission. Delayed original and replay converge through provider same-ID/same-fingerprint idempotency to at most one logical external effect; stale owners cannot observe or finalize.

test_cases.statement: Exercise current observation authority denial, write-authority revocation, proposal/reference expiry, key revocation, missing/mismatched snapshot/trusted-store state and every material capability/binding/policy incompatibility across observation-only and retry paths.
test_cases.oracle: Observation denial occurs before provider lookup. Authorized observation can continue after expiry/key revocation without granting write. Retry fails closed unless every current write check passes; temporary authority denial preserves approved, material mismatch remains stale/non-executable, and missing/mismatched routing state remains typed non-terminal rather than failed.

test_cases.statement: Race current-lease, stale-lease, changed-generation and already-terminal reconciliation callers under deterministic PostgreSQL lock barriers and skewed non-database clocks.
test_cases.oracle: Fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time decides strict staleness. Results are exactly ExecutionNotStale, one Applied takeover, ExecutionFenced, or persisted terminal outcome; generation increments once and stale owner observation/finalization writes are absent.

test_cases.statement: Inject provider observation unavailable, timeout, not-found, malformed/unknown result, found success and every found closed rejection at application and HTTP seams.
test_cases.oracle: Unavailable/timeout/malformed/unknown map to ReconciliationIndeterminate 202; not-found maps to ProviderOutcomeNotFound 202; neither changes lifecycle or grants retry. Only success and approved closed rejections terminalize, with exact closed public fields and no private leakage.

test_cases.statement: Crash after provider commit before PostgreSQL observation and crash after executing commit before provider receipt; restart Knora and SQLite independently and repeatedly reconcile.
test_cases.oracle: Committed provider outcome finalizes without a duplicate; no-receipt path remains non-terminal until safe stale takeover/retry, always reuses logical identity/fingerprint, and produces at most one provider effect across restarts.

test_cases.statement: Reconstruct append-only audit after takeover, observation-only denial/success, write retry denial/success, fencing and terminal finalization.
test_cases.oracle: Audit contains actor/authority decisions, binding snapshot, generations, leases, provider observations, retry decision and terminal result while excluding raw routing, envelope bytes, keys, credentials and secrets; SQLite outcome remains independently authoritative.

test_cases.statement: Run focused M4.4 recovery tests, complete repository pytest, Ruff, Compose and clean Alembic upgrade plus downgrade/re-upgrade on the exact candidate.
test_cases.oracle: All focused, regression, static, composition and migration checks are green on the exact candidate SHA.

command_projections.statement: Clean PostgreSQL recreation and Alembic upgrade/downgrade/re-upgrade with pinned worktree runtime.
Focused Issue #78 and full repository pytest with worktree-pinned PYTHONPATH and sequential PostgreSQL execution.
Ruff and Docker Compose configuration verification.

required_evidence.statement: Provider-first call ordering and zero-call observation-denial evidence for every current Workspace/resource authorization branch.
PostgreSQL takeover CAS rows with fresh post-lock time, expected generation, one winner, exact owner/deadline transition and stale-owner observation/finalization fencing.
NoAdmission first-admission and AdmissionOutstanding byte-identical replay evidence, both retaining one logical ID/fingerprint and at most one provider effect under delayed-original and retry races.
Separate observation-authority and write-authority matrices covering expiry, key revocation, snapshot/trusted-store faults, temporary authority denial and every material compatibility mismatch.
Independent SQLite ledger state before/after Knora restart for not-found, success and every closed rejection, plus both crash windows and repeated reconciliation without duplicate effects.
Exact application/HTTP non-terminal and terminal projection allowlists, append-only audit reconstruction, candidate SHA and governed verification totals/exits.
